stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs Snap Nine-Day Inflow Streak as Ether ETFs Keep Rising
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted a net outflow, ending nine straight days of inflows. Spot Ether ETFs kept taking in new money over the same stretch. Decrypt reported the divergence on August 30.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows show how institutional money is shifting between Bitcoin and Ether right now.
whatToWatch: Next day's flow data, to see if the Bitcoin outflow is a one-day blip or a new trend
Whether Ether ETFs keep their inflow streak going
questions: What caused the pullback from Bitcoin ETFs on this day?
Will Ether ETFs keep outperforming Bitcoin ETFs in flows?

stories.title: Cronos Halts Network After Tectonic Exploit Estimated at $75 Million
stories.summary: The Cronos network stopped block production after an exploit hit the Tectonic lending protocol. Cointelegraph put early loss estimates near $75 million. The cause and full scope of the exploit are still under review.
stories.whyItMatters: A full network halt after a DeFi exploit is a serious incident that can hit user funds and trust in the chain.

Whether affected users get reimbursed
questions: How did the attacker exploit Tectonic?
Will the $75 million estimate hold up, and can the funds be recovered?

stories.title: Mid-Tier Bitcoin Treasury Firm Bets Entire Reserve on a 30-Day Reset Price
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a mid-tier corporate Bitcoin treasury tied its entire BTC reserve to a single price set to reset after 30 days. The report does not name the firm or explain the full mechanism. Details on the structure and its risk remain limited.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how far some smaller corporate treasuries will go with a concentrated bitcoin bet, a risk worth watching as more firms copy the treasury-company model.
whatToWatch: The firm's identity, if disclosed
What happens when the 30-day reset price arrives
questions: Which company made this bet?
What happens to the reserve if Bitcoin's price falls before the reset?

stories.title: Circle's Allaire Touts 'Internet Financial System' as cirBTC Holds Just 40 BTC

stories.whyItMatters: The contrast raises a fair question about how much real traction Circle's Bitcoin-linked product has, despite its stablecoin scale.
whatToWatch: Whether cirBTC holdings grow from here
Any new product details Circle discloses
questions: Why has cirBTC attracted so little Bitcoin so far?
What does Circle plan to do to grow it?

stories.title: Polygon Quietly Patched Security Flaws in Two Hard Forks Before Disclosing Them

stories.title: Russia's Sberbank Eyes USDT Loans, Questions Demand for the Digital Ruble
stories.summary: Sberbank, Russia's largest bank, is reportedly considering loans denominated in USDT, Cointelegraph reports. The bank also voiced doubts about demand for Russia's digital ruble. Details on the loan product's launch or scale are not yet available.
stories.whyItMatters: A major state-linked bank turning toward a dollar-pegged stablecoin, while doubting its own country's CBDC, is a notable signal for stablecoin adoption under sanctions.
whatToWatch: Whether Sber actually launches USDT-denominated loans
Progress, or lack of it, on the digital ruble rollout
questions: How would USDT loans work under current sanctions and capital controls?

stories.title: Proposed Treasury Rule Would Force US Exchanges to Audit Foreign Stablecoins or Delist Them
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that the US Treasury has proposed a change to GENIUS Act rules. The change would require US exchanges to audit foreign-issued stablecoins or remove them from listings. The proposal has not been finalized.
stories.whyItMatters: This could reshape which stablecoins US exchanges can offer, with direct impact on liquidity and access for non-US issuers.
whatToWatch: The public comment period on the proposed rule
Whether Treasury finalizes the change
How exchanges respond if it passes
questions: Which specific stablecoins would be affected?
What would the audit requirement actually involve?

stories.whyItMatters: It shows regulators are willing to pursue insider-trading cases in prediction markets, a sector increasingly tied to crypto trading platforms.
